## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, tibble, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("01_Preprocess/02_Quantification/a_script/02_quantify.qmd")
```

## Read measurements and protein estimates

`dpcQuant()` takes about 100 minutes, so `02_quantify_run.R` runs it and this notebook reads the
checkpoint. The checkpoint must have used every filtered precursor; if filtering changes, rerun the
script.

```{r read}
y <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "01_Filtering", "c_data", "precursors_filtered.rds"))
checkpoints <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "quant_runs")
proteins <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_0.7.rds"))
stopifnot(sum(proteins$genes$NPrec) == nrow(y))
```

## Missingness

In DIA data, low-intensity precursors go missing more often: each precursor's proportion missing
against its mean observed intensity.

```{r ave-vs-mis}
plotAveVsMis(y)
```

## Fit the detection curve

The detection probability curve (DPC) gives the probability that a precursor is observed as a
logistic function of its true intensity. The `dpc()` default is `dpcCN()`, the complete-normal
estimator the limpa FAQ recommends for noisy data.

```{r dpc}
dpcest <- dpc(y$E)
plotDPC(dpcest)

dpc_parameters <- tibble(intercept = dpcest$dpc[1], slope = dpcest$dpc[2])
round(dpc_parameters, 3)
```

The fitted slope, `r round(dpcest$dpc[2], 3)`, sits below the 0.7 to 0.9 band the limpa FAQ calls
typical for DIA-NN with match-between-runs. The FAQ's advice for that case is the project's choice
for the primary run: "If `dpcCN()` doesn't give a value in that range, it would be reasonable to
run `dpcQuant()` with a preset value `dpc.slope=0.7`." Standard errors or hit counts alone do not
show which slope is right, so the fitted slope is kept as a sensitivity run (below and in
`02_Differential`).

## Roll-up

`dpcQuant()` rolls precursors up by `Protein.Group` into a complete matrix with a standard error
per value, which `dpcDE()` later uses to predict each protein's variance. The checkpoint holds
`r format(nrow(proteins), big.mark = ",")` protein groups from `r format(nrow(y), big.mark = ",")`
precursors. Its curve, slope preset and intercept estimated:

```{r used-curve}
round(proteins$dpc, 3)
```

## Detection filter

`filterByDetection()` keeps a protein detected in at least `n.samples` samples, here the smallest
group size. Its help page leaves the threshold to the analyst. The count runs across all samples,
so it does not guarantee detection within any one group.

```{r detection}
group_sizes <- table(proteins$targets$group)
detected <- filterByDetection(proteins, n.samples = min(group_sizes))
proteins <- proteins[detected, ]

detection_summary <- data.frame(
  before = length(detected), kept = sum(detected), dropped = sum(!detected),
  minimum_samples = min(group_sizes)
)

group_sizes
detection_summary
```

## Normalisation

Cyclic loess removes abundance-dependent differences between samples in the protein estimates;
DIA-NN normalised only the precursors. Smyth recommends quantile or cyclic loess normalisation of
limpa protein quantifications when sample differences are technical
([Bioconductor support](https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9163187/#9163221)).

```{r normalise}
unnormalised <- proteins$E
proteins$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(proteins$E, method = "cyclicloess")
```

Densities before and after, then mean-difference plots for the sample whose median sat furthest
from the others.

```{r normalise-plots}
#| fig-height: 8
sample_medians <- apply(unnormalised, 2, median)
worst <- which.max(abs(sample_medians - median(sample_medians)))
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plotDensities(unnormalised, legend = FALSE, main = "Before cyclic loess")
plotDensities(proteins$E, legend = FALSE, main = "After cyclic loess")
plotMD(unnormalised, column = worst, main = paste(colnames(unnormalised)[worst], "before"))
plotMD(proteins$E, column = worst, main = paste(colnames(proteins$E)[worst], "after"))
```

Cyclic loess subtracts an abundance-dependent offset without rescaling, so the standard errors
still apply; the fitted offset is treated as known.

## Blood index

Haemoglobin beta and alpha (HBB, HBA1), set aside in `01_Filtering`, measure how much blood a
biopsy holds. `dpcQuant()` estimates both with the same detection curve as every other protein; the
blood index is the mean of the two log2 estimates, centred. The contamination load from
`01_Filtering`, the share of signal the contaminant filter removed (about 95% haemoglobin and
albumin), joins the sample table for reference; later stages model the blood index.

```{r blood}
haemoglobin <- readRDS(
  here("01_Preprocess", "01_Filtering", "c_data", "haemoglobin_precursors.rds")
)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(haemoglobin), colnames(proteins)))
haemoglobin_estimates <- dpcQuant(
  haemoglobin, "Protein.Group", dpc = proteins$dpc, verbose = FALSE
)
blood <- colMeans(haemoglobin_estimates$E)
proteins$targets$blood <- blood - mean(blood)

contamination <- read_xlsx(
  here("01_Preprocess", "01_Filtering", "c_data", "01_filter.xlsx"), "sample_contamination"
)
proteins$targets$contamination <- contamination$pct_signal_removed[
  match(proteins$targets$sample_id, contamination$sample_id)
]
stopifnot(!anyNA(proteins$targets$contamination))
```

Correlation of the two haemoglobins, Spearman correlation of the blood index with contamination
load, and the median blood index per group:

```{r blood-checks}
round(cor(haemoglobin_estimates$E[1, ], haemoglobin_estimates$E[2, ]), 3)
round(cor(proteins$targets$blood, proteins$targets$contamination, method = "spearman"), 3)
round(tapply(proteins$targets$blood, proteins$targets$group, median), 3)
```

## Check protein estimates

`dpcQuant()` writes the precursor count as `NPrec`, though its help page says `NPeptides`.

```{r quality}
protein_quality <- tibble(
  protein = rownames(proteins),
  gene = proteins$genes$Genes,
  n_precursors = proteins$genes$NPrec,
  prop_observed = proteins$genes$PropObs,
  mean_log2 = rowMeans(proteins$E),
  mean_standard_error = rowMeans(proteins$other$standard.error),
  mean_n_observations = rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations)
)
summary(protein_quality[c("mean_log2", "mean_standard_error", "prop_observed")])
```

`plotMDSUsingSEs()` places samples by their protein profiles, weighted by the standard errors.
limma's `plotMDS()` redraws it coloured by treatment (open T1, filled T2) and labelled by
participant, saved as `02_quantify_mds.pdf`; then the share of the first coordinate participant and
group explain.

```{r mds}
#| fig-height: 10
mds <- plotMDSUsingSEs(proteins, plot = FALSE)
treatment_colours <- c(BFR = "#D55E00", HLRT = "#0072B2")
draw_mds <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 1))
  plotMDS(mds, col = treatment_colours[proteins$targets$treatment],
    pch = c(T1 = 1, T2 = 16)[proteins$targets$timepoint], main = "MDS of protein abundance")
  legend("topright", c(names(treatment_colours), "T1", "T2"), bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
    col = c(treatment_colours, "grey30", "grey30"), pch = c(16, 16, 1, 16))
  plotMDS(mds, labels = proteins$targets$participant, cex = 0.6, main = "Labelled by participant")
}
draw_mds()
pdf(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "b_reports", "02_quantify_mds.pdf"),
  width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
draw_mds()
invisible(dev.off())
round(sapply(proteins$targets[c("participant", "group")], function(f) {
  summary(lm(mds$x ~ factor(f)))$r.squared
}), 3)
```

## Slope sensitivity

The sensitivity run quantifies against the fitted curve. It gets the same detection filter, which
reads only observation counts and so keeps the same proteins, and the same normalisation. Each
run's curve and mean standard error, then the median absolute abundance difference;
`02_Differential` compares the contrasts.

```{r slope-sensitivity}
#| eval: !expr file.exists(file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_fitted.rds"))
sensitivity <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_fitted.rds"))
sensitivity <- sensitivity[filterByDetection(sensitivity, n.samples = min(group_sizes)), ]
sensitivity$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(sensitivity$E, method = "cyclicloess")
stopifnot(identical(rownames(sensitivity), rownames(proteins)))

tibble(
  role = c("primary", "sensitivity"),
  intercept = round(c(proteins$dpc[1], sensitivity$dpc[1]), 3),
  slope = round(c(proteins$dpc[2], sensitivity$dpc[2]), 3),
  mean_standard_error = round(c(
    mean(proteins$other$standard.error), mean(sensitivity$other$standard.error)
  ), 3)
)

round(median(abs(proteins$E - sensitivity$E)), 4)
```

The section runs only when `quant_runs/proteins_slope_fitted.rds` exists:

```sh
Rscript 01_Preprocess/02_Quantification/a_script/02_quantify_run.R --sensitivity
```

## Save results

Models that take a design (`dpcDE()`, fry) read `proteins.rds` and carry the blood index as a
covariate. `proteins_adjusted.rds` has the blood effect removed by `removeBatchEffect()`, group and
participant protected, for steps that take no design (singscore, WGCNA, mixOmics).

```{r write}
out <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data")
saveRDS(proteins, file.path(out, "proteins.rds"))
adjusted <- proteins
adjusted$E <- removeBatchEffect(
  proteins$E, covariates = proteins$targets$blood,
  design = model.matrix(~ 0 + group + participant, proteins$targets)
)
saveRDS(adjusted, file.path(out, "proteins_adjusted.rds"))
write_xlsx(
  list(
    samples = as.data.frame(proteins$targets),
    dpc_parameters = dpc_parameters,
    detection_summary = detection_summary,
    protein_quality = protein_quality
  ),
  file.path(out, "02_quantify.xlsx")
)
```
